fixes.explanation: I get why you'd think that. But the LORD says the opposite: "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Nobody gets to hang up the apron yet. Joshua is old and well along in years, and the job is still open.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) That covers all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. He puts Himself right in that sentence as the One who drives them out. Then He gives Joshua a different job: divide the land by lot.

Joshua is Israel's leader, so he's a natural guess. But look at who the LORD names here: "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) He puts Himself right in that sentence. Joshua's job in the verse is to divide the land by lot.

That's it! The LORD says, "Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) So this land is for nine tribes plus half of Manasseh. The other half of Manasseh had already received its inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). Keep an eye on that half, friend.

Twelve tribes is the number everybody remembers. But the LORD says this land goes "…to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) The other half of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had already received the inheritance Moses gave them beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). So they weren't waiting on this land.

Reuben and Gad are a fair guess, since they do come up in this chapter. But they had already received their inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). This land is for "…the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) Reuben and Gad already had their boxes packed.

False is right, baker! The text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) The verse doesn't say they were driven out. It says they dwell among the Israelites.

Yes! "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) Levi is the tribe Moses gave no inheritance of land. The verse names the food offerings as their inheritance instead, and says it's just as He had promised.

Gold sounds like a nice inheritance, but this passage doesn't give it to Levi. It says, "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) That's the inheritance the verse names for them. Moses gave them no land.
